'''Solaran''' ({{lang|sol|𐍖𐰇𐰴𐰤}}), also known as '''Solra''', is the vernacular language of [[Solara]]. It evolved from the ancient [[Solra|Elder Tongue]] used in temples and governmental meetings, maintaining the same lexical core while simplifying sound contrasts and grammar. Solaran is the language of daily life, commerce, and popular culture, learned natively by all Solaran children, while fluency in the Elder Tongue remains the domain of priests, scribes, and high officials.

== Phonology ==

Solaran preserves a set of '''19 consonant phonemes''', including a deep‑throated stop /q/ and a flowing lateral fricative /ɬ/. The vowel inventory has been pruned to '''nine short vowels'''; distinctions of length and nasalisation once present in the Elder Tongue have vanished in everyday speech. Stress normally falls on the second‑to‑last syllable.

== Script ==

The '''Sunline Alphabet''' is the standard writing system for Solaran:
* A '''left‑to‑right alphabet''' containing '''26 symbols''' derived from the classical script
* Vowels are full letters written on the same line as consonants
* Spacing divides words; punctuation marks indicate pauses and questions

While the Elder Tongue's abugida persists for liturgy, Sunline dominates street signs, contracts, and newspapers. For a detailed description of the alphabet, see [[Solaran Alphabet]].

== Grammar ==

{| class="wikitable"
|+ Grammar Overview
! Category
! Solaran Mechanism
|-
| '''Word order'''
| Subject–Verb–Object by default
|-
| '''Nouns'''
| No case endings; relations shown with short prepositions (*ta* = to/for, *di* = of, *na* = at/in, *ke* = with). Plural marked by '''‑s''' or by context.
|-
| '''Verbs'''
| Invariant root; tense and person expressed with auxiliaries placed before the root.<br> *mi ofer* "I offer", *mi na ofer* "I offered", *mi sha ofer* "I will offer".
|-
| '''Adjectives'''
| Follow the nouns they modify (*san haloim* "sun eternal").
|-
| '''Questions'''
| Rising intonation and optional sentence‑final '''‑ka'''.
|}

== Sociolinguistic Role ==

Solaran embodies everyday Solaran identity. While official edicts are still proclaimed first in the Elder Tongue, a Sunline Solaran translation follows immediately so the entire populace understands. Schools teach reading and writing exclusively in Sunline for the first six years; instruction in the Elder Tongue begins only for students entering priestly or administrative tracks.

A '''Language Office''' updates a yearly *Lexicon of Solaran* to:
* Codify spelling
* Coin native terms for new technologies
* Discourage uncontrolled borrowing from neighbouring states

Dialect variation flourishes—coastal accents soften /q/ to /k/, mountain accents shift /ɬ/ toward /s/—yet mutual comprehension remains high.
